To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

SO motility is coordinated with duodenal motility, that SO dysfunction causes biliary-type pain, that SO and biliary pressure are elevated during phase 3 and that gastrectomy and proximally located duodenal transections affect sphincter pressure.
SO contractions are cyclic, and that SO motility can be affected by the duodenal phase 3 MMC and by gastrectomy.

SO motility is cyclically coordinated with the MMC, that the pressure elevation during phase III may contribute to the pain in patients with sphincter of dyskinesia and that SO manometry can be used as an objective tool for the diagnosis and treatment of patients with sphincteric dysfunction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physiology of the SO and biliary tract.
the physiology of the sphincters of Oddi and ampulla, with the goal of understanding the pathophysiology, diagnosis, and therapy of diseases of these structures.
the physiology and pathophysiology of the sphincters of Oddi and pancreatic duct.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
manometric studies of the sphincteric system of the biliary tract are of great interest in the understanding of biliary physiology.
the sphincter is a complex structure, which is not only important for biliary flow, but also for the regulation of duodenal flow.
the human SO is a complex, highly regulated, and integrated part of the digestive system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SO motility and pressure are important in the pathogenesis of biliary diseases and that SO manometry has become a valuable tool in the evaluation of patients with biliary pain.
the sphincter is a complex structure with a variety of motility patterns, which can be recorded and studied using manometry.
manometry of the SO and biliary tract is an important tool in the study of motility disorders of the biliary tract.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SO motility is coordinated with the MMC of the duodenojejunal complex and may be responsible for the cyclic changes of biliary pressure.
the sphincter plays an active role in biliary dynamics, and its dysfunction can be diagnosed by SO manometry.
SO manometry can be used to diagnose biliary dyskineisa and to predict the outcome of endoscopic sphincterotomy in patients with biliopancreatic disorders.
